newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil oil imports to hit trade balance - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil oil imports to hit trade balance - paper.

text.p: Oil imports will hit Brazil's trade balance this year as growing domestic demand outstrips the country's production and refining capacities, the local Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper reported on Saturday.
The value of oil imports should reach $5.5 billion to $6 billion this year, compared to $4.6 billion in 1995.
In September higher oil imports were cited as the reason for a larger than expected trade deficit of $655 million.
The rise in demand has even surprised state oil company Petrobras, Folha said.
An 18 percent increase in petrol consumption between October 1995 and September 1996 has cost Petrobras $52.5 million more than it expected in the first half alone.
Original forecasts were for imports totalling 500,000 cubic meters in the first six months of this year. In reality however 800,600 cubic meters were required.
Imports of other products such as diesel and MTBE were also higher, the newspaper said.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
